The legacy completions API carries the user text in a `prompt` string rather than a `messages` list. This checks the router uses that string as the text it routes on: 'escalate' is present, and this policy sends requests containing 'escalate' to cloud.

A `prompt` may also be a list of strings, which the router should join into one text. This policy routes to cloud only when the text holds both 'alpha' and 'omega' — one is in the first list item, the other in the second — so reaching cloud confirms every item was included (reading only the first item would drop 'omega' and it would stay local).

A `prompt` list can contain non-text items (here an object); the router should ignore those and use only the strings. The object holds the word 'escalate', which this policy would route to cloud under a different rule if the object were turned into text. Because the request instead matches on 'alpha' + 'omega' (the two string items), the object was ignored, not read.
The Responses API can carry the user text as a plain `input` string. This checks the router uses that string as the text it routes on: 'escalate' is present, so it routes to cloud.

An `input` may be a list of role-tagged messages; the router routes on the last user message's text. Here that text is an 'input_text' part (the Responses API spelling of a text part, handled like chat's 'text'), so 'escalate' routes to cloud.

When an `input` list has no role-tagged user message, the router falls back to concatenating every plain-string item into one text. Both 'alpha' (first item) and 'omega' (second) must appear to reach cloud, so routing there confirms every item was concatenated — otherwise it would stay local.

The routing input is the last user turn, not the whole conversation. The earlier user turn says 'escalate' and the last one does not, so escalate-rule misses and the request falls to default (local). Reading the whole history would match escalate-rule -> cloud.

A request carrying messages alongside prompt and input routes off messages only. The last user turn holds no keyword while both prompt and input say 'escalate', so falling to default (local) shows neither of the other fields was read.
With no messages, prompt is read and input ignored. The prompt matches alpha-omega-rule while the input would have matched the earlier escalate-rule, so matched_rule shows which field was read.

note: A multi-key leaf is an implicit all whose children run in op-name order, not in the order the keys are authored. The rule authors regex first, yet the trace reads keywords_any, min_chars, regex.
keywords_any comes first and is false, so the implicit all short-circuits and neither min_chars (which would pass) nor regex is evaluated: the trace holds one entry.

regex is the last child, so a failing regex is reached only after min_chars passed: the trace holds three entries ending in regex. Were regex evaluated second, the all would short-circuit there and min_chars would be missing.
'shared' matches both rules; the engine takes the first, routing to cloud (not edge).
'only2' matches just the second rule; the first is skipped, so it routes to edge.
No rule matches, so the request falls open to default_model (local).
A rule may route to default_model on purpose. Because a rule matched, matched_rule is set and default_used stays false, even though route_to is the same 'local' as fail-open-to-default.
A matched rule copies its non-empty nested outputs bag (object + array + number) verbatim into the Decision.
Without route_trace the Decision carries no trace key: the matched-request trace is empty and route_decision_to_json drops the field.
An explicit route_trace:false behaves exactly like omitting it — no trace key.
route_trace:true records one entry per evaluated leaf; 'alpha' makes the any's first child true, so the regex child is never evaluated and the deterministic leaf carries no score/label/rationale.
The trace accumulates every leaf up to the match: missed any-rule contributes both false children, then all-rule matches and the not(max_chars) child is still traced with its own raw result (false).
all-rule's first child ('charlie') is false, so the all short-circuits and the not(max_chars) child is dropped from the trace; fail-open to default still carries the accumulated trace.
